verdicts.explanation: The paper states that the ionic conductivity of gc-Li42P16S61 is 33.1 mS cm–1 from this work's AIMD with Arrhenius extrapolation to room temperature, and Table 1 lists it under 'Our AIMD'. Null activation energy and synthesis fields are acceptable.

The text gives crystalline Li7P3S11 at 46.9 mS cm–1 as this work's predicted value, used for comparison with gc-Li42P16S61. Origin is computational and the temperature is room temperature, so the record is consistent with the paper.

The paper gives β-Li3PS4 at 14.3 mS cm–1 as a simulated room-temperature value, and says predicted β conductivities are much greater than experiment. The record's computational origin and null secondary fields are consistent.

The text states gc-Li38P24S79 (x = 0.613) has ionic conductivity 3.45 mS cm–1 and activation energy 0.282 eV, and Table 1 gives the same values under 'Our AIMD' with the RT column in mS cm−1. The temperature is room temperature and origin computational, as recorded.
